classification.habit: Tall glabrous shrub or small soft-wooded tree, 2–4 m high.
classification.habitat: Waste land, riverbanks and around habitations; widely cultivated as an oilseed crop.
classification.distribution: Throughout India, mostly growing wild and also cultivated, notably in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh.

identification.description: Tall shrub with palmately lobed leaves, prickly three-celled fruits and smooth mottled seeds.
identification.whole_plant: Fast-growing shrub with large palmately lobed leaves, often reddish stems, and spiny capsules in terminal racemes.
identification.root: Light, almost straight with few rootlets; outer surface dull yellowish-brown with longitudinal wrinkles; odourless; taste acrid.
identification.stem: Hollow, glaucous, green or reddish, with prominent nodes and leaf scars.
identification.leaf: Large, alternate, peltate, palmately 5–11-lobed, lobes serrate; petiole long.
identification.flower: Monoecious, in terminal panicled racemes; male flowers below with branched stamens, female flowers above with red feathery stigmas.
identification.fruit: Three-celled capsule, globose, usually covered with soft spines, splitting into three cocci.
identification.seed: Oblong, one face convex, 1–1.5 cm long, glossy, grey to brown and variously mottled, with a prominent caruncle.

therapeutics.dose: Mula kwatha 50–100 ml; Eranda taila 5–15 ml (virechana 15–30 ml)
therapeutics.anupana: Warm milk or warm water for Eranda Taila; Shunthi kwatha in Amavata.
therapeutics.precautions: Seeds contain the highly toxic protein ricin and must not be chewed or eaten raw; only the oil and processed preparations are used. Purgative doses cause fluid and electrolyte loss.
therapeutics.contraindications: Eranda Taila in purgative dose is contraindicated in pregnancy, intestinal obstruction, acute abdomen, inflammatory bowel conditions and in children without supervision.

ब्रध्नश्वासकफानाहकासकुष्ठाममारुतान् ।
एरण्डपत्रं वातघ्नं कफक्रिमिविनाशनम् ॥५५॥
मूत्रकृच्छ्रहरं चापि पित्तरक्तप्रकोपणम् ।
वातार्यग्रदलं गुल्मं बस्तिशूलहरं परम् ॥५६॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Castor oil consists mainly of ricinoleic acid glycerides, while the root contains the alkaloid ricinine; the seed protein ricin is highly toxic and does not pass into properly expressed oil.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Castor plant used for joint pain, digestive issues and vata-related disorders.
recognized_uses: Amavata and Vatavyadhi, including Gridhrasi and Katishula
modern_information.safety_notes: Castor oil is a stimulant laxative; avoid in pregnancy and obstruction. Raw seeds are poisonous because of ricin.
